questions.prompt: Where does the lesson put rules such as "`Title` is required, max length 100", and why?
options: As `[Required]` and `[MaxLength]` attributes on `TaskItem`, so the rules sit next to the data
In a `TaskConfig : IEntityTypeConfiguration<TaskItem>` class in Infrastructure, so the domain entity stays clean
In the controller, before calling the service
Directly inside `OnModelCreating`, so every rule is in one file
questions.explanation: The goal is to keep Domain clean and move DB rules to configuration classes, one per entity. Putting everything inside the DbContext is called out as bad.

source.section: Fluent API configurations with separate configuration class

questions.prompt: What does `modelBuilder.ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(typeof(AppDbContext).Assembly)` give you over calling `modelBuilder.ApplyConfiguration(new TaskConfig())` for each entity?
options: It makes the configurations apply only in Development
It picks up every configuration class automatically, so it scales as the project grows
It removes the need for `DbSet<T>` properties
questions.explanation: Listing each configuration by hand is manual and error-prone; scanning the assembly picks up all of them.

source.section: Fluent API configurations with separate configuration class

questions.prompt: Put what happens internally, from entity to database, in order.
questions.explanation: The configuration classes shape the model the DbContext builds; `dotnet ef migrations add` turns that model into SQL and `dotnet ef database update` creates the schema.

questions.prompt: For a PATCH/update endpoint, which AutoMapper call does the lesson recommend?
options: Either one; they behave the same
Neither; AutoMapper can't be used for updates
`_mapper.Map(objProject, dto);`, because it merges into the existing instance and keeps values that aren't provided
questions.explanation: Mapping into an existing instance only overwrites what the source provides. Creating a new instance fills missing values with defaults, which would overwrite existing data on update.

source.section: Map into existing instance vs create new instance

questions.prompt: The source property is shown below, and the destination's `Id` is a non-nullable `Guid`. What value does the destination `Id` get after mapping?
questions.explanation: The destination can't hold `null`, so AutoMapper maps it to `Guid.Empty`, which prints as all zeros, even though the source was `null`.
